Pace model

Each green lap's sector times at the Barcelona race, fitted with an effect and a tyre-wear slope per car plus tyre compound and age, lap number and traffic, allowing for an offset that holds through each stint. Gaps are at a tyre age of 9 laps on the hard, with the fastest-looking car's luck (81 ms) taken off. Fitted on odd laps it predicts even ones to 0.29 s (a car's own median lap: 0.71 s). ± is one standard error; Model health shows how often the bench's intervals held the truth. Not enough green laps for an estimate (fewer than 10): Stroll.

okRace pace, sector gaps93 %1.05± 0.06 s0.52 sresolved

Each model is run on synthetic races with the confounders the feed carries switched on: different lines and commitment per driver, tyre wear that differs by team, fuel, track evolution, dirty air and ~4 Hz sampling for grip; car-specific wear and offsets that hold for a whole stint for pace. 95% covers: how often the stated 95% interval held the true value (pass at 90% or more). Error ÷ ±: spread of the errors over the stated uncertainty (1 is honest; pass at 1.25 or less). A quantity is resolved when the bench backs its intervals and a typical ± is under a third of the spread between teams or cars; interval only when the differences are real but rankings are uncertain; not resolved when the data can't tell them apart. Pace gaps are at a tyre age of 9 laps on the hard, with the fastest-looking car's flattering luck (81 ms) taken off.
